artists.biography: Mint Field is Mexican duo Amor Amezcua and Estrella Sanchez from Tijuana. Comprised of 21-year-olds Estrella Sanchez (vocals & guitar) and Amor Amezcua (drums & synths), Mint Field’s sound is organic, spacious, and inhabited by specters that lurk behind rhythms, where Estrella’s angelic voice evokes a supernatural world of beauty and melancholy. Their record, Pasar De Las Luces, first for LA-based Innovative Leisure Records, is “a compilation of our lives from two years ago to now” says the band. Since recording an initial EP in 2015 in their hometown of Tijuana, Mint Field have played Coachella, SXSW and have extensively toured the US and Mexico. In the summer of 2017 the band traveled to Detroit to record with producer Christopher Koltay. “We had a much clearer idea of what we wanted and we had the tools to make it. When we recorded [our debut EP] Primeras Salidas, it was a homemade album and we didn’t know what we were doing.” This time, they managed to channel their inspirations and influences to transmit sentiments of profound sorrow, nostalgia and immaculate beauty…revisiting sounds from the past to make them contemporary. Mint Field’s vision comes alive on Pasar De Las Luces ‘s 13 immaculate tracks that nod to everything from dream pop to fuzz-saturated shoegaze. Album opener “El Parque Parecía No Tener Fin,” is a melodic number with haunting melodic lines where we can appreciate their post-punk tendencies. “Ciudad Satélite” has woven harmonies and crescendos that detonate into a flurry of feelings anchored by a dramatic bassline. “Quiero Otoño De Nuevo” goes full krautrock and is like an introverted, reflective and delicate Neu!. ”Cambios Del Pasar” borrows the distorted and imperfect guitar sounds of ‘90s indie bands like Yo Lat Tengo. “Nada Es Estático y Evoluciona” develops from minimalism into a silent scream and “Club De Chicas” is probably the peppiest song of the bunch. The whole record has a unique sound that makes it stand apart from projects by contemporaries. Sanchez and Amezcua not only show the potential of influencing even younger fans, but of also defining themselves as stand alone voices in emotional music. Although they have a foot in the past, they never let themselves get caught by nostalgia; they reinterpret the best of what the past has to offer in order to better express their feeling in the present. It’s a timeless quality that can surely take them far into the future. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Mint Field’s debut album Pasar De Las Luces, released on February 23, 2018, via Innovative Leisure, is a defining statement in the Mexican psych rock scene. The Tijuana-based duo—Estrella del Sol and Sebastian Neyra—craft a sound that blends dream pop, shoegaze, and subtle trip-hop elements, resulting in an atmospheric and introspective listening experience. The album’s hazy textures, reverb-drenched guitars, and melancholic melodies evoke a sense of nostalgia and urban solitude, reflecting on the emotional landscapes of daily life. Its tracklist, including standout songs like “Ojos En El Carro” and “Boötes Void,” showcases the band’s ability to balance experimental soundscapes with accessible songwriting.

As Mint Field’s first full-length release following their 2015 EP, Pasar De Las Luces established the group’s signature style and marked their arrival on the international stage. The album received positive critical attention for its immersive production and emotional depth, with reviewers highlighting its “otherworldly immersion” and nuanced approach to rock and dream pop. While not a commercial blockbuster, the album solidified Mint Field’s reputation as innovators within the Latin American rock scene and set the foundation for their subsequent work.
